reels.a11y_body:
To spot Reels and Shorts, the add-on uses Android's Accessibility service to check which screen Instagram, YouTube and short-video apps are showing, and which address your browser has open, then presses Back for you.

It only looks at those apps and browsers, doesn't read your messages, pages or what you type, and nothing leaves your phone.

Android needs a few taps to allow it: AdWizz shows each step.
reels.a11y_title: Allow the AdWizz add-on to see which screen is open?
reels.blocked: Google Play Protect blocked the add-on because it can use Accessibility. To install it anyway: open the Play Store, tap your profile picture → Play Protect → ⚙ settings, turn off "Scan apps with Play Protect", tap Try again here, then turn scanning back on.
reels.desc: Leaves Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts as soon as they open, in the apps and in browsers like Chrome, and closes short-video apps (TikTok, Moj, Josh, Likee and more). With protection on, TikTok and similar sites are blocked in every app too.
reels.install_body:
Blocking Reels and Shorts uses Android's Accessibility service, so it comes as a small separate app, "AdWizz Add-on" (about 20 KB). AdWizz downloads it from the same place as AdWizz itself and checks it's signed by AdWizz.

Google Play Protect may block it, because it can use Accessibility. If it does, AdWizz shows what to do.
reels.needs_a11y: Needs one more step: turn on "AdWizz Add-on" in Accessibility settings.
reels.title: Block Reels & Shorts
settings.always_on_desc: Turn on Always-on for AdWizz so protection survives reboots and the system restarts it if it's killed.
settings.bypass_desc: Catches apps that hard-code Google/Cloudflare/etc. DNS or use DNS-over-HTTPS to them.
settings.excluded_desc: Some apps (banking, streaming, games) refuse to work when a VPN is on. Excluded apps skip AdWizz completely: they won't see the VPN, but their ads aren't blocked either.
settings.generated_desc: Catches brand-new ad domains like pgjlctmswgnwf.com before any list has them. If a site breaks, tap it in Recent activity on Home to allow it.
settings.malicious_desc: Phishing, scam and malware sites, and scripts that mine crypto-currency in your browser.
settings.pdns_desc: If Private DNS is set to a specific hostname (e.g. dns.google), Android sends DNS over TLS directly and skips AdWizz.
settings.pdns_title: Private DNS must be Off or Automatic
settings.trackers_desc: Analytics, tracking pixels, fingerprinting scripts, disguised first-party trackers and phone-maker telemetry (Samsung, Xiaomi, TikTok…).
settings.update_found: v{version} is available — see the top of the screen
tips.huawei: On Huawei/Honor: Battery → App launch → AdWizz → Manage manually, all switches on.
tips.oppo: On Oppo/Realme/OnePlus: App settings → Battery → Allow background activity, and allow Auto launch.
tips.other: Set AdWizz's battery usage to Unrestricted so the system doesn't stop it in the background.
tips.samsung: On Samsung: App settings → Battery → Unrestricted, and keep AdWizz out of 'Sleeping apps'.
tips.vivo: On Vivo/iQOO: Settings → Battery → Background power consumption → allow AdWizz, and enable Autostart.
tips.xiaomi: On Xiaomi/Redmi/POCO: App settings → Autostart ON, and Battery saver → No restrictions. Also lock AdWizz in Recents.

firewall.title: Block apps' internet
firewall.desc: Picked apps can't look up any address, so they can't reach their servers or show ads. Works while protection is on. Apps that connect by IP address alone can still get through.
firewall.block_app_desc: Every look-up it makes is blocked
addon.intro: YouTube and Spotify serve ads from the same servers as videos and songs, so no DNS blocker can stop them. The AdWizz add-on (a small separate app using Accessibility) handles them on the phone instead.
addon.youtube_desc: Taps "Skip" the moment it appears and mutes ads that can't be skipped. YouTube and YouTube Music.
addon.spotify_desc: Mutes Spotify while an ad plays and turns the sound back on for the next song. Needs "Device broadcast status" on in Spotify: AdWizz shows you how.

addon.installed_off: Add-on v{version} is installed, but switched off in Accessibility.
addon.pause_hint: An app acting up while the add-on runs? Pause it, or turn it off for apps that refuse to open with Accessibility on (some banking apps).
addon.turned_off: Add-on turned off. Turn it back on in Accessibility settings.
uninstall.title: Uninstall
uninstall.desc: Removes AdWizz and its add-on. Android asks you to confirm each one.
settings.sponsored_desc: Removes "Sponsored stories" and "Around the web" boxes (Taboola, Outbrain and similar) in every app and site. With the add-on, also covers sponsored cards in YouTube and Instagram.
spotify.setup_body: AdWizz can only tell when Spotify plays an ad if Spotify shares what it's playing. Turn this on once:

spotify.step3: 3. Turn on "Device broadcast status", then play a song.

https.title: HTTPS filtering (browsers)
https.desc: Browsers send their traffic through AdWizz, which looks inside it: blocks ad URLs, removes YouTube's ads on youtube.com (incognito too) and hides ad and sponsored boxes on pages. Apps like the YouTube and Spotify apps don't accept this and pass through untouched (the add-on handles those).
https.confirm_body:
AdWizz will create its own security certificate. Once you install it as trusted, AdWizz can read and filter what your browser loads, on this phone only: nothing is sent anywhere, and the certificate's private key stays locked in your phone's secure hardware.

Banking and other sites still work, but they will show AdWizz as the issuer of their certificate. Turn this off and remove the certificate any time.
https.ready: ✓ Certificate installed: your browser's traffic is being filtered.
https.not_ready: One more step: install AdWizz's certificate. Until then, nothing is decrypted.
https.step2: 2. Open security settings, then find "Install a certificate" (on Samsung: More security settings → Install from device storage).
https.step3: 3. Choose "CA certificate", tap Install anyway, and pick AdWizz-HTTPS.crt from Downloads.
https.firefox: Firefox: turn on Settings → About Firefox (tap the logo 5 times) → Secret settings → Use third party CA certificates.
https.remove_hint: Turned it off? Remove the certificate in Settings → Security → Trusted credentials → User.
